piece_title: The faction system — joining, ranks, refusals, discipline, and the continuation nobody judged

critic.successor_note: Re-judging round 1 after RECOVERY-20260814 restored three W1-20 files. Part 1 establishes what the round-1 critic could and could not see and rules that W1-20-r1 STANDS: it ran on 2026-08-08 and the recovered material was authored on 2026-08-10, so it was never judging against a hole. What the deletion cost was round two, and the recovery is two files short — 091a6cec also reverted part of game/src/engine.js and all of orchestration/status/W1-20.json, neither of which a file-level sweep can see.

build.dirty_note: A dozen agents commit concurrently. No faction data file — faction-gates.json, the 12 faction quest files, faction-discipline.json, factions/registry.json, faction-refusals.json, faction-reactions.json — and no file under game/src/sim/quest/**, game/src/sim/stealth/** or game/src/sim/dialogue/** was dirty in the live tree at any measurement. The null-control arm ran in a hard-linked clone under /tmp with only faction-gates.json unlinked and rewritten; the repository's own faction-gates.json was md5'd before and after the clone was built and is byte-identical.
build.contention: node tools/contention.mjs was consulted before every browser run. It returned WAIT twice (load 4.53-4.86 per core against a 4.0 ceiling, 3-4 instances against a 6 ceiling); on both occasions I did the static census and the data work and returned when it cleared. NO TIMING FIGURE IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE IN THIS VERDICT — every number is a count, a rank, a reputation, a disposition, a gold price or a boolean.

bifurcation.note: A data, text and measurement piece. Nothing here is judged by how it looks; every observation is a count, a state transition, a spoken string or a boolean. No screenshot is cited.

reference_items.native_scale: Mean of six sub-scores, then hard-gated. 'We lose = score < 6, or any hard fail.'
reference_items.native_verdict: NO HARD FAILS, where round 1 had two. All eight lines carry 18 quests across all eight rank bands (mean 2.25/rank against a 2.0 floor); deceit present on every line and first at rank <= 3 on all eight; dirty_work first at rank 4 on all eight; succession at rank 7 on all eight; stakes monotonic with no band dropping >= 2.0 against the band below, spanning 2 to 10; 12-18 quests per line move a rival faction's reputation against a target of >= 6 and a hard fail below 3. Sub-scores: rank ladder depth 10, quest volume 5 (18 is the floor of the item's 18-23 band against a 24-28 target), task-kind progression 9, stakes curve 8, corruption reveal 5 (present and early, but the dissenter NPC's authored record is in an unloaded file — see the secondary findings), rival contradiction 10. Mean 7.83, held at 7.5.
reference_items.why_not_ten: Volume is exactly 18 per line against a 24-28 target — the item's own 5/10 band. 70 of 144 faction quests have stakes == rank + 2, which is the 'spreadsheet rather than a story' signature the item's own How-we-lose section names, though real variance does exist (rank 2 carries stakes 4, 5, 6 and 8). Two lines place a politics quest at rank 0 (Q-DOCK-01, Q-MAG-07) against a 5-6 target. And the corruption reveal, which the item wants to be a PERSON, points at people whose authored voice is in a file the engine does not load.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Six more quests per line to reach the 24-28 band; stakes chosen per quest rather than derived from rank; move the two rank-0 politics quests to rank 5-6 or re-tag them; and load the authored dissenter records so the reveal has a voice.
reference_items.justification: RI-QST01 scores 7.5 on the strength of corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-20-r2/r2-census.json, which counts every metric the item's own comparison method specifies over game/data/quests/**: 18 quests on each of the eight lines across all eight rank bands (mean 2.25/rank against a 2.0 hard-fail floor), deceit present on every line and first at rank <= 3 on all eight, dirty_work first at rank 4 on all eight, succession at rank 7 on all eight, no stakes band dropping >= 2.0 against the band below, and 12-18 rival-touching quests per line against a target of >= 6. Zero of the item's four hard-fail clauses fire. Round 1 measured five volume hard fails and one honesty hard fail on the same instrument class; all six are gone.

reference_items.native_scale: Band table, 0-10, plus hard fails. Aggregation: band.
reference_items.native_verdict: The band table alone would read 7-8: eight complete 8-row requirement tables gating on reputation AND an attribute AND two favoured skills AND a world state, verified live (a character with 120 reputation and no skills is refused rank 7 on all eight lines, each naming the specific skill and its threshold); exclusivity implemented and biting (joining the Wet Ledger locks three factions and 54 quests); expulsion and readmission implemented, characterised per line and NOT uniform (three distinct prices, per-line prose, a shortfall line). Held at 5 by two stated failures the band table does not price. (1) THE CEILING: ranks 5, 6 and 7 are unreachable in any save on the_dockhands, the_drowned_court, the_ixtu_vakh and the_rootkeepers, because the world_state each rank names is raised by no quest resolution anywhere in game/data. 21 authored quests, including every succession quest on those four lines, cannot be opened. (2) Greedy single-save reachability is 87.5% against the item's stated fail line of 75% — three of eight joins close no door at all.
reference_items.why_not_ten: The ceiling; 87.5% reachability; reputation slack 2.19x-3.71x on all eight lines against a 1.6x warn ceiling; offences_tolerated and on_permanent absent from all eight discipline rows (two of the three fields §7 names); and deep_kin's favoured-skill set byte-identical to the_xul_aneekh's, which §3 forbids above 3 shared skills.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Twelve world_flags entries on quests that already exist at the right ranks; exclusivity declarations on the three lines that close nothing; halve the reputation awards or raise the rank-7 requirement; add offences_tolerated and on_permanent; resolve deep_kin one way or the other.

reference_items.native_scale: Five axes, min-over-axes. 'Coupling measured' scores 0 if any model has coupling == 0. Failure threshold: any coupling == 0 on a model the piece's own reference items require to act.
reference_items.native_verdict: Three of the four models this piece ships have a named world-side consumer and were driven through it: the rank ladder (sim/quest/gate.js:209; sim/dialogue/disposition.js factionTerm reached from Engine.npcDisposition via Engine.talkTo; sim/stealth/theft.js:26 and :74 reached from engine.js:10201 and :10286), the refusal voice (QuestEngine.open's rank-gate path), and expulsion/readmission (sim/quest/machine.js:299-311, :667). The fourth has NO world-side reader at all: game/data/factions/registry.json is fetched at boot by game/data/index.json and read by nothing in game/src. Its only reader was Engine.factionAccess(), which does not exist at HEAD — running the piece's own recovered instrument gives 'TypeError: engine.factionAccess is not a function'. coupling = 0, fail-closed. SEPARATELY, the rank ladder itself couples on only 7 of 8 lines: the_dockhands is absent from faction-reactions.json's aliases and matrix, so its representative sits at disposition 47 at ranks 0, 2, 4 and 7 while the other seven move 21-24 points.
hard_fails: coupling == 0: game/data/factions/registry.json (8 records, 5,984 bytes, in the data index) has no world-side reader. grep -r factionRegistry game/src -> 0 hits. grep -r factionAccess game/src -> 1 hit, game/src/harness/api.js:2165.
coupling == 0 on one line of a coupling model: the_dockhands has no entry in faction-reactions.json aliases or matrix, so faction rank reaches no NPC disposition for that faction.
reference_items.why_not_ten: A model whose only reader is the harness is an orphan by this item's definition, and the delivery report names exactly that method as its consumer. The merge did not create the orphan; it made it audible.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Restore three lines from 9ed28905 (the loader branch, the install, factionAccess) so the model is readable, then give it a world-side caller — something must ask for the services list. Add the_dockhands to faction-reactions.json. Then re-run node tools/quests/w1-20-builder.mjs and node tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-live.mjs.

checks.observed: Nothing in this piece touches frames, hitboxes, stamina, poise or animation. Souls wins inside the fight; there is no fight here.

No level scaling and no level gating. Every one of the 64 rank rows across eight ladders gates on reputation, an attribute, two favoured skills and a world state; the census asserts no row carries a level, souls or quest_count key and none does.
Rank changes what the law calls theft, where you may walk and the war-brood disposition shift. It changes no archetype, statblock or moveset.
Souls are levelling only. No faction gate, refusal, rank or discipline row reads or writes soulsHeld.

Gold is the currency. Readmission is priced in gold (400/900/1200 across the eight lines) and rank never is — driven live: setGold(0) is refused with the shortfall in the sentence, setGold(99999) is readmitted.

score.band_label: FAIL against the wave-1 gate of 7.0. RI-MTH07's coupling clause is binary and one of the four models this piece ships has no world-side reader, so the item is 0 and the min over items is 0. The verdict does not turn on that reading: strike RI-MTH07 out entirely and the min is 5.0, set by RI-QST03's rank ceiling, and it is still FAIL. Both numbers are published.
score.confidence_note: Every figure is a count, a rank, a reputation, a disposition, a gold price or a boolean; none is a timing measurement, so the box's load touches none of them. The two live arms ran on the same build minutes apart. The static findings are reproducible with grep.

weights.note: min-over-axes within each item, min-over-items overall. No axis is averaged away. RI-MTH07's own scoring table makes 'any coupling == 0' a 0 on the Coupling axis and the item aggregates min-over-axes, so 0 is the item's construction rather than my preference. The unclamped alternative — the min over the remaining five prose axes — is 5.0.

RI-QST03: ranks 5, 6 and 7 are unreachable in any save on four of the eight ladders, because the world_state each of those ranks requires is raised by no quest resolution anywhere in game/data. 21 authored quests, including every succession quest on those four lines, cannot be opened. Measured live (a fully-skilled character stops at rank 4 on all eight lines) and confirmed by the null control (the same character reaches rank 7 on all eight when the world_state column is flattened).
RI-QST03: greedy single-save reachability is 87.5% against the item's stated fail line of 75%; three of eight joins close no door at all.

RI-MTH07, second instance: the_dockhands is absent from faction-reactions.json's aliases and matrix, so rank in that faction reaches no NPC disposition — its representative is flat at 47 across ranks 0, 2, 4 and 7 while the other seven lines move 21-24 points.
AR-1 and AR-2 both pass; RI-QST01 has ZERO hard fails where round 1 had two; the remedies are buildable, named and re-measurable. This is FAIL and not VOID.
hard_fails: RI-MTH07 coupling == 0 on the registry-services model. grep -r factionRegistry game/src -> 0 hits.
RI-MTH07 coupling == 0 on one line of the rank model: the_dockhands has no faction-reactions.json entry.
RI-QST03 completability, through the world_state column: 4 of 8 ladders have ranks 5-7 that no save can reach. Reproduce: node tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-census.mjs (QST03.ceiling.*).

biggest_gap.what: RI-QST03 §B puts a world-state requirement on ranks 5, 6 and 7 of every ladder. On four of the eight lines the world states named are raised by nothing: the_dockhands (dockhands_gang_held, dockhands_wharf_decided, dockhands_harbourmaster_vacant), the_drowned_court (court_yard_held, court_tally_decided, court_crown_vacant), the_ixtu_vakh (sapcutters_well_cut, sapcutters_buyer_decided, sapcutters_cutter_vacant) and the_rootkeepers (rootkeepers_sapwell_kept, rootkeepers_chapter_decided, rootkeepers_voice_vacant). `grep -rl dockhands_gang_held game/data/` returns exactly one file, faction-gates.json. The other four lines are clean — ledger_gate_held, assize_seal_held and the Deep-Kin/Xul-Aneekh states are each raised by a real quest resolution. Measured live: a character given every favoured skill at 100, every favoured attribute at 100 and 400 reputation reaches rank 4 on all eight lines and stops, held by the world state; in the null control, with that column flattened, the same character reaches rank 7 on all eight. So the live arm establishes what holds everyone at 4 and the static grep establishes that on four lines nothing can ever move it. 21 authored quests are stranded above the ceiling — 4 on the Dockhands, 6 on the Drowned Court, 6 on the Ixtu-Vakh, 5 on the Rootkeepers — including every succession quest on those lines.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Round 1's failure was visible: a line with one quest on it. This one is invisible. Every static check passes, every quest exists, the census is green, and the player simply finds that the Rootkeepers stop promoting them and nobody says why. It is Ruling W1's shape exactly — an aggregate (RI-QST03 §4's 'earnable reputation >= the rank-7 requirement', which passes on all eight lines) standing in for something a player meets one rung at a time. And it deletes the beat RI-QST01 says the whole ladder exists to arrive at: the player taking the seat.

remedy.acceptance: node tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-census.mjs returns zero QST03.ceiling.* hard fails, AND node tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-live.mjs reports A4.lines_reaching_rank_ge_5 = 8 of 8 on the shipping tree (it is 0 of 8 today).
remedy.action: Twelve world_flags entries on quests that already exist at the right ranks. For each of the four lines: give its rank-4 or rank-5 quest a resolution that raises the line's *_held flag, its rank-6 quest one that raises *_decided, and its rank-7 quest one that raises *_vacant. The four carried lines already show the pattern — copy game/data/quests/faction-wet-ledger.json's ledger_gate_held.

evidence_notes: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-20-r2/r2-live-null-control.json — A4.lines_reaching_rank_ge_5 = 8 of 8 with the world_state column flattened
grep -rl dockhands_gang_held game/data/ -> game/data/quests/faction-gates.json (one file, and it is the gate itself)

secondary_observations: the_dockhands is absent from game/data/dialogue/faction-reactions.json altogether — no alias, no matrix row — so rank in the Dockhands reaches no person in the world. npc-porter-eeja sits at disposition 47 at ranks 0, 2, 4 and 7 while the other seven representatives move 21-24 points across the same span. Fix: two lines of JSON.

A locked player is told they have been admitted. QuestEngine.open() refuses correctly and records 'The Imperial Assize will not deal with you: you are The Wet Ledger' — but the sentence the player hears is voice.kind 'welcome': 'The roll is amended. You are an officer of this court.' Measured on all five locked lines. The voice is chosen from gate.allowed, which is the RANK gate; the exclusivity lock never reaches the mouth. Fix: sim/quest/refusal.js must consult rivalry_locked before gate.allowed.

Rank moves the disposition number but never the greeting band: across rank 0 to 7 the greeting cell is constant on all eight lines (110, 135, 15, 15, 260, 235, 210, 40). The player hears a different sentence at rank 7, but it is the same band's rotation.
Three of eight joins close no door at all — deep_kin, the_dockhands, the_rootkeepers. Two of those three are lines W1-20 opened.

deep_kin is still one body under two ids and the world still says two contradictory things about it: its own 18-quest ladder, its own discipline row and its own registry seat, and a join refusal that says 'It is the same people and the same door.' Its favoured-skill set is byte-identical to the_xul_aneekh's, which RI-QST03 §3 forbids above 3 shared skills.
Reputation slack is 2.19x-3.71x on all eight lines against the item's 1.6x warn ceiling.

offences_tolerated and on_permanent are absent from all eight discipline rows — two of the three fields RI-QST03 §7 names. Without offences_tolerated there is no second offence, so the tier structure that distinguishes a Thieves-tier from a Morag-Tong-tier institution is not expressible.

The round-1 critic's residual fail-open is still live at game/src/ui/system.js:1358 (it was :1167 on 08-08; the line moved, the defect did not): fits: (m.widest_px || 0) <= t.rect[2] + 0.5. So are the nine tools/analysis/audio-budget.mjs rows and tools/quests/critic-faction-r2.mjs:352. Six days, no owner.

The dialogue-words agent's finding that '257 of 336 NPC records carry actor names no starting topic is written for' does NOT bite W1-20 as I can measure it. Across all 408 NPC records in game/data/npcs/**, 7 carry an actor with no topic INFO (spellwright x4, enchanter x3), and all eight faction representatives answer 9 of the 9 starting topics and carry 2-4 topics of their own.

quest-witnesses.json is absent from game/data/index.json, and it does NOT orphan a faction consequence — all 16 of its ids also exist in the loaded game/data/npcs/mainline.json. But the two records are different people. The authored one is the corruption reveal in a voice ('The stopper mark was cut before the phial crossed the...'), the right race, and the topic little-advice. The loaded one is a generated shell whose topics are the quest title as a free string ('a phial for the blind man'), which is not a topic id in any of the 21 topic files. Walked up to in the running game, the four I tested greet the player with generic town filler and two of the four say the identical sentence: 'You're from here, or near enough. Mind the wagons.' The dissenter is in the world and has nothing to say — RI-QST01's named 'No dissenter' loss mode in disguise, touching 13 faction quests across four lines. The fix is one index line PLUS removing the 16 colliding shells, and that is W1-18's call.

tools/control-clone.mjs cannot build a clone of this tree: it refuses any path that is neither a regular file nor a directory, and tools/node_modules/.bin/ is full of symlinks ('control-clone: tools/node_modules/.bin/pixelmatch is neither a regular file nor a directory (mode 120777)'). The null-control clone was made by hand with cp -al. That is a real gap in a tool HAZARDS §5a recommends.
path_to_ten: The systems are ahead of the content standing on them, still, and the content is no longer the emergency it was in round 1. In order: (1) twelve world_flags entries to unbrick ranks 5-7 on four lines; (2) three lines of engine.js restored from 9ed28905 plus a world-side caller, so the registry is a model the game reads; (3) two lines of faction-reactions.json so the Dockhands exist to the disposition system; (4) refusal.js consulting rivalry_locked before gate.allowed, so a locked player is told they are locked rather than welcomed; (5) exclusivity declarations on the three lines that close nothing, to bring single-save reachability under 75%; (6) six more quests per line to reach RI-QST01's 24-28 band. Every one of those is small, and none of them is a system.

arbitration_questions.question: When a merge reverts part of a file that still exists, no file-level recovery sweep can see it. RECOVERY-20260814 restored 74 files and missed both of W1-20's in-file reverts — 18 lines of game/src/engine.js and the whole of orchestration/status/W1-20.json. Should the recovery method gain a second pass that diffs each accidental-deletion commit's SURVIVING files against the side it claimed to merge?
arbitration_questions.why_it_matters: The in-file revert was the more damaging of the two here: the deleted files were an instrument and a report, and the surviving-file revert was the game's only reader of an entire data file. Both came from the same commit. The cheapest detector turned out not to be git at all — it was booting the game and watching a harness verb throw.

corpus_extended.gap: §4 checks that a ladder is completable and does it entirely on the reputation column: 'hard fail if earnable for any faction is less than that faction's rank-7 reputation requirement.' All eight lines pass it — and four of them cannot be climbed past rank 4, because the WORLD-STATE column has no completability check at all. The column was added to §B's binding table and never reached §4's comparison method, so the item's own 'Unreachable ranks' loss mode is reachable with every stated check green.
corpus_extended.proposed: A fifth clause in §4: every world_state named by a rank row must be raised by at least one quest resolution in the book. One line of the same jq. Reference implementation: the QST03.ceiling.* rows in tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-census.mjs.

method_deviations.deviation: Built two instruments: tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-census.mjs (static, 126 rows against RI-QST01 and RI-QST03's own comparison methods, plus a grep-based consumer audit) and tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-live.mjs (live, two arms). Declared under RULES 24.
method_deviations.why: No tool in the tree measured the world_state ceiling, the registry's consumers, or what an entity does when a rank moves after the continuation landed. The round-1 critic's instruments were re-run rather than rebuilt (RULES 3) and answer a different set of questions.

method_deviations.deviation: Re-ran the round-1 critic's tools/quests/critic-w1-20-reach.mjs at HEAD rather than rebuilding it, and ran the recovered builder instrument tools/quests/w1-20-builder.mjs at HEAD.
method_deviations.why: RULES 3. reach.mjs reproduces its round-1 findings at HEAD (exit 0, positive control green, 8/8 rows on three lines). w1-20-builder.mjs crashes, and the crash is the finding.

method_deviations.deviation: The null-control clone was built with cp -al by hand rather than with tools/control-clone.mjs, which refuses this tree.
method_deviations.why: control-clone.mjs errors on tools/node_modules/.bin's symlinks. The clone was verified the way that tool verifies its own: the repository's faction-gates.json was md5'd before and after and is byte-identical, and only the unlinked copy was written to.

unmeasured: Whether the eight representatives are reachable ON FOOT. Round 1 measured two of four new recruiters unreachable (npc-porter-eeja at 31.97 m from every bearing) and the continuation's delivery row 14 is BUILT / NOT_RUN on exactly that. It is still NOT_RUN. My live arm confirms all eight exist and can be spoken to once populateSettlement has run; it says nothing about walking there.

Blind prose judgement of the escalation writing. Delivery rows 2, 12 and 13 remain NOT_RUN. Ruling W2 says the gate for them is a person reading the quests, not a chart, and this verdict scores the escalation SHAPE from the data and explicitly does not score the writing.

Whether the topics the eight representatives carry actually surface in a conversation at each rank. I measured the greeting and the greeting cell, not the topic list — talkTo's topics_offered came back undefined in my rows and I did not chase it.
Whether the 21 quests stranded above the rank ceiling are otherwise well-formed. They validate and they are counted; nobody has read them, because nobody can reach them.
The theft and trespass consumers on the six lines that own no faction_interior anywhere in the populated world. Round 1 measured that census; I did not re-run it.

self_audit.aggregation_note: Ran the recovered builder instrument at HEAD before judging anything, and re-ran the round-1 critic's reach instrument rather than reading its report.
self_audit.instrument_falsification: The null control falsified MY OWN checks, which is the finding worth reading. I marked five live checks `discriminating: true`. Under the plausible wrong answer — every faction accepts everyone and refuses nobody, with all eight ladders, every rank name, every favoured set, every exclusivity declaration and every line of refusal prose intact — only TWO flipped: A2 (7 refusals carrying a number -> 0) and A4 (rank 4 on all eight -> rank 7 on all eight). A1 and A3 were inert because I read r.ok, a field factionRefusal does not return, so both arms scored 8/8; B1, B2, B3, C1 and D1 test models the control deliberately does not touch, so marking them discriminating was my error. All three failures are reported in the verdict and fixed in the tool, which now reads r.kind. A separate first-pass failure is also reported: all eight talkTo calls threw 'nobody by that name is in the world' because I had not called populateSettlement, and I nearly published that as a defect of the build.
self_audit.self_audit_note: blind_done_where_required is TRUE in the sense that no blind pack was assigned to this round and none of the three items judged here is blind_pair: yes for the measurements taken — RI-QST01 is blind_pair: yes for its §7 prose test, which is NOT_RUN and is declared in unmeasured[] rather than scored. ran_every_assigned_method is TRUE for RI-QST01 §§2-6 and RI-QST03 §§1-7 and RI-MTH07 §B; RI-QST01 §7 (the blind rank-band test) was not run and its sub-score is not claimed from it.

notes: PART 1 RULING, reversible: W1-20-r1 STANDS as written and is not superseded on its own commit; W1-20-r2 is the current verdict of W1-20. The dispatch's premise that the round-1 critic judged against a hole is not what the dates say — r1 ran on 2026-08-08 and the recovered material was authored on 2026-08-10 by 9ed28905, then partly deleted sixteen minutes later by 091a6cec. What the deletion cost was round two, not round one. WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: a copy of 9ed28905's material on the branch before 2026-08-08. The object database has one authoring commit per path and it is dated 08-10.

THE RECOVERY IS TWO FILES SHORT, and no file-level sweep could have known. 091a6cec also reverted 18 lines of game/src/engine.js (the factions/registry.json loader branch, the this.factionRegistry install, and the 19-line Engine.factionAccess) and the whole of orchestration/status/W1-20.json (from builder-delivery-complete with ten added files_touched entries, back to the pre-continuation record). Both files still exist, so RECOVERY-20260814's per-path method is blind to them. Worth adding to HAZARDS: the cheapest detector for an in-file revert is not git, it is booting the game and watching a harness verb throw.

THE DOWNSTREAM DOCUMENTS ARE STALE, and this is the cheap fix nobody has made: node tools/dispatchable.mjs W1-20 still advises a critic to push on 'RI-QST01 volume over the four new lines', against a build where every line has carried 18 quests since 2026-08-10; and GAP-W1-faction-ladders-are-doors-onto-empty-corridors is still carried open against a tree where its five hard fails are zero.

reports/w1-20/builder-continuation.json is on disk and deliberately not landed — reports/.gitignore excludes *.json under reports/ and the original was force-added past that rule. RECOVERY-20260814 left the decision to W1-20's owner and this verdict does the same; the blob is permanent at 9ed28905:reports/w1-20/builder-continuation.json.

I did NOT file a gap_closure for GAP-W1-faction-ladders-are-doors-onto-empty-corridors, and the reason is a rule rather than a doubt: the ledger ignores a closure filed in the same wave that opened the gap ('Closure must come from a later wave's critic'). Its five volume hard fails and its honesty hard fail all measure ZERO at HEAD — 18 quests across 8 full rank bands on every one of the eight lines, deceit on every line — and that is recorded here so a wave-2 critic can close it in one re-measurement: node tools/quests/critic-w1-20-r2-census.mjs, rows QST01.volume.*, QST01.bands.*, QST01.meanPerRank.* and QST01.deceit.*.
